source.title: Online Normalization for Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Vitaliy Chiley; I. Sharapov; Atli Kosson; Urs Köster; R. Reece; S. de la Fuente; Vishal Subbiah; Michael James

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares normalization methods in training experiments, including Batch Normalization and no normalization, and reports learning curves. It uses a different method and reports validation metrics rather than training error.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR ResNet experiments compare Online Normalization with Batch Normalization and other normalizers, but do not include a no-normalization comparison. The text says Online Normalization had the best validation performance; it does not report training classification error. The FC and U-Net figures include no-normalization comparisons, but their curve values are not stated in text.
record.test_reason: The study compares Batch Normalization with no normalization over training epochs in two new settings: a ReLU MLP on Fashion MNIST and U-Net segmentation. These comparisons bear on V6's acceleration claim, although the supplied text rendering does not preserve the curve trajectories sufficiently to determine their direction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Online Normalization competes with leading normalizers, supports settings where some alternatives do not apply, and reduces activation-memory requirements through batch-free normalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests Online Normalization against other normalization methods across classification, segmentation, and language-modeling experiments; it does not reproduce the claim's training-error experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and normalization method vary across experiments; the supplied text also reports multiple normalization methods for several tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: BN gradient estimates differ from the full-dataset gradient by more than 10 degrees at moderate batch sizes, with network weights fixed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization introduces batch-size-dependent gradient bias.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing normalization statistics can produce exponential activation growth in a fixed 100-layer network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Errors in normalization statistics can amplify across depth unless activations are bounded or explicitly scaled.

fits_no_version.finding: Online Normalization matches or exceeds comparison normalizers on several validation metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online Normalization can achieve competitive predictive performance without batch-based normalization.

record.problems: The ImageNet ResNet-50 experiment reports a single run. Several relevant learning-curve comparisons are figure-only in the supplied text, without numeric values or explicit BN-versus-no-normalization descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified. CIFAR ResNet validation comparisons omit a no-normalization condition, and their validation metrics do not measure the versions' stated training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, and dependence on model size or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, their learning speeds, and trainable depths.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability training.
Maximum tolerated learning rates and the Fixup comparison. Optimized learning-rate selections do not establish stability limits.

record.verdict_notes: No V6 verdict is justified from the recoverable numbers: final validation performance does not determine learning speed. The unreadable trajectories are an evidence limitation, not evidence that acceleration is absent. Online Normalization's superiority over BN also does not establish BN's effect relative to no normalization.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, and model size are not tested.
Teacher-student ReLU networks and spurious minima are not tested.
Depth effects and identity shortcuts are not compared.
Initialization schemes and trainable depth are not compared.
Learning-rate stability thresholds and curvature are not measured.

The paper reports learning curves for architectures with Batch Normalization and no normalization, but gives no explicit textual result comparing their speed. Figure-only comparisons are recorded in rows; no claim verdict can be assigned from those curves without reading values.

rows.subject: three-layer fully connected network, 500+300 HU
rows.operation_detail: Compared training trajectories with Batch Normalization and no normalization on Fashion MNIST.
rows.note: The plot includes Batch Normalization and no normalization, but the supplied text gives no numeric comparison between these curves.
rows.check: The measure is validation accuracy over epochs, not unspecified accuracy. Figure 14 supplies median accuracy values across 400 runs: BN 88.3% versus no normalization 88.8%. These final validation results do not establish which method gains accuracy faster; Figure 11's curve trajectories cannot be recovered from this text rendering.

rows.subject: U-Net
rows.operation_detail: Compared training trajectories with Online Normalization, Batch Normalization, and no normalization on a synthetic shape dataset.
rows.note: The plot includes Batch Normalization and no normalization. The text says Online Normalization achieved the best Jaccard similarity, but does not state the BN versus no-normalization result.
rows.check: Figure 14 supplies median Jaccard values across 50 runs: BN 0.976 versus no normalization 0.961. These final segmentation scores do not establish acceleration. The recipes also use separately optimized learning rates: BN 0.04 versus no normalization 0.6. Figure 10's curve trajectories cannot be recovered from this text rendering.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
